title: Saying number names in order
keyIdea: Counting words always come in the same order: one, two, three, four, five, then six, seven, eight, nine, ten. Say every number once, with no skips and no repeats. Songs, rhymes and stairs help the order stick. You can count back too: five, four, three, two, one.

kid: Let us count. One, two, three, four, five! The numbers go in the same order every time. Two comes after one. Three comes after two.
Do not skip one. One, two, four is a slip. It goes one, two, three, four.
Say each one just once. Then keep going: six, seven, eight, nine, ten!
We can count back too. Five, four, three, two, one. Blast off!
adult: This topic, for ages 2 to 3, is about reciting the counting words in the right order: first one to five, then on to ten. It is the counting string that later counting, adding and number sense are built on. Saying the words in order is not yet the same as counting objects; matching one word to each thing comes next.

Children learn the list like a song. The first few words are fixed early, then a child may have a stable but unusual part, such as one, two, three, five, six, which they say the same way each time. That is normal. Keep modelling the full list in songs and on the stairs, and they will correct it with practice.

Common mistakes: skipping a number (one, two, four), saying a number twice (two, two, three), getting lost after five (six, eight), and rushing so the words blur together. Be careful not to drill. Slow down, count together, and pause so your child can fill in the next word.

In the lab your child climbs five stairs saying each number, drags the missing number into a counting train, spots where Silly Bear skips or repeats a number, hops a frog to ten, and counts back from five to launch a rocket.

familyTip: Count the stairs every time you go up or down: one, two, three, four, five. Sing Five Little Ducks and Once I Caught a Fish Alive. Sometimes stop before a number, like one, two, …, and let your child say three.

practice.hint: Say it out loud: one, two, …
practice.explain: Three comes after two. One, two, three.

practice.prompt: Count with me: {n}, {=n+1}, … what comes next?
practice.hint: Say the next number. Do not jump over one.
practice.explain: After {n} and {=n+1} comes {=n+2}. Each number comes once, in order.

practice.prompt: Bear says: one, two, four. What did he miss?
practice.explain: Bear missed three. It goes one, two, three, four.

practice.prompt: We climb the stairs. We are on step {n}. What is the next step?
practice.hint: One more step up. Say the next number.
practice.explain: Step {n}, then step {=n+1}. We go up one number at a time.

practice.prompt: Count back for the rocket: five, four, … what comes next?
practice.hint: Going back, the numbers go down.
practice.explain: Five, four, three, two, one. Three comes next when we count back.

pool.prompt: Which one is in the right order?
pool.hint: Start at one. What comes next?
pool.explain: One, two, three is the right order. The order is the same every time.

pool.hint: Say it from the start: one, two, three, four, …
pool.explain: Five comes after four. One, two, three, four, five.

pool.prompt: Bear says: one, two, two, three. What went wrong?
pool.hint: Listen for a number that comes more than once.
pool.explain: Bear said two twice. Each number comes once: one, two, three.

pool.hint: Keep going one at a time. No skipping.
pool.explain: After {=n+2} comes {=n+3}. Every number gets its turn.

pool.hint: After five the names are six, seven, eight, nine, ten.
pool.explain: Eight comes after seven. Six, seven, eight, nine, ten.

pool.prompt: The frog hops on stone {n}. Which stone is next?
pool.hint: The frog hops forward one stone. Say the next number.
pool.explain: Stone {n}, then stone {=n+1}. Each hop is the next number.

pool.prompt: Count back: three, two, … what comes next?
pool.hint: Counting back goes down to one.
pool.explain: Three, two, one! Counting back goes down.

pool.prompt: Mia counts: one, two, three, five. Which number did she miss?
pool.hint: Say it slowly: one, two, three, …
pool.explain: Mia missed four. It goes one, two, three, four, five.

visual.caption: Say the numbers as you tap: one, two, three, four, five.

lab.caption: Flagship lab: climb and count to five, fill the gap on a number train, catch Silly Bear's slips, hop to ten and count back for a rocket.
